next_step: Closed - lost to customer's decision to self-host (vLLM/TGI/TensorRT-LLM). Archive opportunity; keep for re-engagement if budget/champion resurfaces.
competitor_win: Customer implemented internal stack based on vLLM + TextGenerationInference + TensorRT-LLM optimizations
notes:
Opportunity notes:
- Customer: Avalon SignalWorks (industrial telemetry vendor). Evaluated Redwood for chat + reranking pipelines feeding anomaly detection dashboards.
- Primary drivers for self-host decision: cost predictability at scale, control over GPU stack, ability to run quantized models on local infra, residency and audit needs. Quote from Eng lead: "We can shave significant margin by running vLLM/TGI on our NVIDIA fleet and control kernel tuning ourselves."
- Security team ran hosted security questionnaire; flagged data residency and custom KMS policies as blockers. They declined hosted compliance concessions.
- Finance: initial ARR target looked ok but board instituted a hiring/freeze that reprioritized infra spend to capital (CapEx) rather than SaaS OpEx.
- SE involvement: Riya ran 3 architecture workshops; provided latency/cost estimates vs self-host scenarios. Customer still preferred full-stack ownership.
- Timeline to close: slipped several times, final decision Aug 2024 to self-host.
- Follow-up plan: document gap analysis (what Redwood would need to offer to win back), track internal infra milestones, re-engage after first-quarter run-rate proof.
- CRM style notes: short, choppy on calls - "no-hosted, moving infra in-house", "security wants KMS in their zone", "want to own kernel tuning".
timeline: 2024-03-15: Intro demo (hosted API + routing) - AE + SE present
2024-04-02: Security questionnaire submitted; Redwood SOC2/infra materials shared
2024-06-20: Cost vs self-host analysis provided by SE
2024-08-10: Final decision - customer chooses self-host (vLLM/TGI/TensorRT-LLM) - opportunity lost
